apitest.yaml:
# apitest conformance payload — the user-mode sibling of ../kmtest.
#
# The apitest binaries themselves (*_apitest.exe + their testdata) are staged to
# reactos/bin by add_rostests_file when the build dir has ENABLE_ROSTESTS=ON
# (`./vibeos-cli build --arch X --rostests`; note this is the FULL rostests
# switch, ~128 executables, not the cheap ENABLE_ROSTESTS_KMTESTS the kmtest
# payload rides on). This payload grafts:
#   * apitest-sweep.exe into the All Users Startup folder — a native
#     GUI-subsystem exe, because a .cmd there dies silently: explorer's
#     AutoStartupApplications walk uses ShellExecuteExW, which never spawns
#     cmd.exe for a script.
#   * apitest-suites-{arch}.txt staged in-guest as bin/apitest-suites.txt.
#     GENERATED, not committed — `python3 tools/payloads/apitest/gen_suites.py
#     --arch X` derives it from the binaries the build produced. The kmtest
#     list is committed and that is how upstream's ExPushLock kmtest went a
#     whole merge without ever being launched, against a sweep reporting
#     `launched=91 ok=91 bad=0`.
#
# Unlike kmtest, the child processes report through wine/test.h's
# winetest_vprintf -> fprintf(stdout), not through the debug serial, so the
# sweep pipes each suite's stdout+stderr and re-emits it as
# [APITEST:<suite>] lines. See sweep.c for why that is the whole reason this
# is a separate runner.
#
# Booting a rostests-less build with this payload fails loudly on serial
# ([APITEST-SWEEP] launch FAILED / FATAL: cannot open ...) — no silent pass.
name: apitest
description: user-mode NT/Win32 API conformance tests (apitests) — piped-stdout sweep autostart

build_hint: "tools/payloads/apitest/build.sh {arch} && python3 tools/payloads/apitest/gen_suites.py --arch {arch}"

binaries:
  - src: tools/payloads/apitest/apitest-sweep-{arch}.exe
    root: image
    dest: ProgramData/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup/apitest-sweep.exe
  - src: tools/payloads/apitest/apitest-suites-{arch}.txt
    dest: bin/apitest-suites.txt
  - src: tools/payloads/apitest/apitest-skip-{arch}.txt
    dest: bin/apitest-skip.txt

test:
  # One process per suite, 300s cap each. ~128 suites, so budget generously:
  # SCM gate + N suites. WALL-CLOCK SECONDS -- and that is load-bearing here:
  # while the drain was an iteration count this sweep, the chattiest payload
  # after procstorm, got 12-28 minutes out of a declared 7200 and was truncated
  # mid-run every single time. Keep any driver's own timeout ABOVE this number,
  # or the driver becomes the real bound and the truncation comes back.
  launch_marker: "[APITEST-SWEEP] done"
  launch_drain_secs: 7200
  # Stop after this much TOTAL SILENCE. A healthy sweep prints a launch/exit
  # pair per subtest and caps each child at 120s, so it is never quiet for long;
  # ten minutes of nothing means the guest or the sweep parent is wedged.
  # Without this a wedge cost the whole 7200s budget -- three rounds in a row
  # sat reading nothing from 19:01 to 21:01. It is also the only signal that
  # positively implicates the GUEST rather than the rig, so the driver's
  # quarantine rule is built on it.
  launch_idle_secs: 600

spec.name: apitest
spec.description: user-mode NT/Win32 API conformance tests (apitests) — piped-stdout sweep autostart

appstorm64.yaml:
# appstorm64 — appstorm's whole sweep as an x86-64 GUEST on arm64: the stock amd64 build of
# every app and applet, run under FEX (wowx64). arm64 only, and only on VIBEOS_FEX=1 media.
#   tools/payloads/appstorm/build.sh amd64   (rebuilt automatically when stale)
#   VIBEOS_FEX=1 VIBEOS_PAYLOAD=appstorm64 ./vibeos-cli build --arch arm64   (needs build-amd64)
#   ./vibeos-cli smoke --arch arm64 --payload appstorm64
# appstorm-amd64.exe autostarts from the StartUp folder as an x86-64 process, so every app it
# launches by name resolves through the guest's system32 -> sysamd64 redirect to the amd64
# copy staged below. appstorm checks each launched process's machine against its own, so an
# app that ran native instead is a FAIL, not a pass.
name: appstorm64
description: appstorm's app and applet sweep, every app the stock amd64 build, under FEX on arm64
arches: [arm64]

build_hint: "tools/payloads/appstorm/build.sh amd64"

binaries:
  - src: tools/payloads/appstorm/appstorm-{arch}.exe
    build_arch: amd64
    root: image
    dest: ProgramData/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup/appstorm.exe
  # The amd64 side-by-side assemblies. An x86-64 process's activation context asks for
  # processorArchitecture amd64, and the arm64 media carries only arm64 assemblies, so every
  # comctl32 v6 / gdiplus activation in a guest failed ("CreateActCtxW failed ... err=2").
  # winsxs is outside system32, so these are found by their own names, not by the redirect.
  - src: dll/win32/comctl32/amd64_microsoft.windows.common-controls_6595b64144ccf1df_5.82.2600.2982_none_deadbeef.manifest
    dest: winsxs/manifests/amd64_microsoft.windows.common-controls_6595b64144ccf1df_5.82.2600.2982_none_deadbeef.manifest
  - src: build-amd64/dll/win32/comctl32/comctl32.dll
    dest: winsxs/amd64_microsoft.windows.common-controls_6595b64144ccf1df_5.82.2600.2982_none_deadbeef/comctl32.dll
  - src: dll/win32/comctl32/amd64_microsoft.windows.common-controls_6595b64144ccf1df_6.0.2600.2982_none_deadbeef.manifest
    dest: winsxs/manifests/amd64_microsoft.windows.common-controls_6595b64144ccf1df_6.0.2600.2982_none_deadbeef.manifest
  - src: build-amd64/dll/win32/comctl32/comctl32.dll
    dest: winsxs/amd64_microsoft.windows.common-controls_6595b64144ccf1df_6.0.2600.2982_none_deadbeef/comctl32.dll
  - src: dll/win32/gdiplus/amd64_microsoft.windows.gdiplus_6595b64144ccf1df_1.0.14393.0_none_deadbeef.manifest
    dest: winsxs/manifests/amd64_microsoft.windows.gdiplus_6595b64144ccf1df_1.0.14393.0_none_deadbeef.manifest
  - src: build-amd64/dll/win32/gdiplus/gdiplus.dll
    dest: winsxs/amd64_microsoft.windows.gdiplus_6595b64144ccf1df_1.0.14393.0_none_deadbeef/gdiplus.dll
  - src: dll/win32/gdiplus/amd64_microsoft.windows.gdiplus_6595b64144ccf1df_1.1.7601.23038_none_deadbeef.manifest
    dest: winsxs/manifests/amd64_microsoft.windows.gdiplus_6595b64144ccf1df_1.1.7601.23038_none_deadbeef.manifest
  - src: build-amd64/dll/win32/gdiplus/gdiplus.dll
    dest: winsxs/amd64_microsoft.windows.gdiplus_6595b64144ccf1df_1.1.7601.23038_none_deadbeef/gdiplus.dll

# The apps and applets appstorm launches, plus everything they import, out of build-amd64.
# rundll32 hosts every applet control.exe opens. The .cpl files and the modules at the END of
# the list are loaded by name at run time, so no import walk finds them:
#   lpk         the language pack user32/gdi32 load by name; refused, they retry on every
#               text call (18929 refusals, each a blocking serial line, in one sweep)
#   apphelp     kernel32's app-compat check at every process create
#   schannel    secur32's TLS provider (rapps's database download is https)
#   rsaenh      the crypto provider schannel's CryptAcquireContext opens by its registry
#               "Image Path", which rsaenh writes itself at registration (rsaenh.rgs), so no
#               INF names it for tools/fex/wow64-closure.py to derive
#   actxprxy    the COM proxy iexplore marshals its browser object through
#   mshtml      ieframe's document object
#   rosbrand    shell32's About-box branding, named by a string literal in shell32
#   dpwsockx    dxdiag's DirectPlay provider
#   batt bthci  device-class property pages devmgmt loads from the class keys
#   msvfw32     comctl32's animation control (SysAnimate32) decodes its AVI through it;
#               refused, cleanmgr's progress dialog never created and cleanmgr waited forever

# NOT FOUND"); that is how each of these was found. winmm's Drivers32 set is derived by
# tools/fex/wow64-closure.py instead.

  launch_marker: "[APPSTORM] done"
  shot_prefix: "[APPSTORM] shot "
  pass_marker: "[APPSTORM] done VERDICT=PASS"
  launch_drain_secs: 7200
  # 1G (the arm64 default) runs out: the FEX guests already resident (x86 Doom and the
  # ladder) leave ~30MB free before the sweep starts, the livecd has no pagefile, and each

  # kernel that bugchecks 0x7A on an exhausted machine rather than failing the allocation.

# Design doc: docs/engineering/payload-harness-design.md
# Bring-up story: docs/engineering/doom-on-vibeos.md
#
# Build-time consumer: tools/payloads/compile.py (staging manifest).
# Test-time consumer: tests/qemu/test_payload.py (interprets `test:` below).
# Enable in an image:  VIBEOS_PAYLOAD=doom ./vibeos-cli build --arch <arch>
#                      (legacy alias: VIBEOS_DOOM=1)

description: doomgeneric (Win32 GDI backend) + shareware WAD — adversarial-compat demo

    dest: system32/doom.exe

autostart:
  - cmd: doom.exe
    mode: demo
    # Run-key emission is blocked on the amd64 ProcessStartupItems fix
    # (task #24 / design doc Workstream A). Until then winlogon's
    # file-presence check (DoomStaged -> TryStartDoom) launches it; staging
    # dest system32/doom.exe is what arms that path.
    via: legacy-winlogon

test:
  # Serial marker proving the launcher actually spawned the exe
  # ([WINLOGON] on arm64 / [USERINIT] on x86 both emit it).
  launch_marker: "doom.exe created"
  launch_drain_secs: 30    # launcher may fire after the boot marker

  xfail:
    i386: >-
      i386 can't load a keyboard layout at boot: LoadKeyboardLayoutW ->
      NtCreateSection(SEC_IMAGE) deadlocks in the i386 Rust MM, so winlogon
      skips it; win32k drops every key at 'NO keyboard layout'. Flip to a
      hard assert once fixed (task #19).

  # Gate 2 — the game is drawing frames (attract demo animates the screen).
  renders:
    settle: 3              # window come-up after boot marker
    gap: 2.0               # seconds between the two compared screendumps
    frame_delta_min: 0.02  # attract demo animates ~50%; tray clock <<0.1%

  # Gate 3 — PLAYABLE: keys reach the game. Click into the window for focus
  # (exercises the mouse chain), then menu-drive a new game; an idle E1M1
  # first-person view is near-static vs the ~50%-delta attract demo.
  input:
    settle: 3
    focus: click-center    # rel-mouse sweep to top-left, recenter, left-click
    drive:
      - keys: [esc, ret, ret, ret]   # menu / New Game / episode / skill
        gap: 0.7
      - wait: 2.0                    # level load + first frame
    oracle:
      frame_delta_static_max: 0.012  # status-bar face + palette dither budget
      gap: 1.5
      survives: true                 # QMP query-status still running at end
    retries: 3             # foreground can lag post-restore; ESC also
    on_retry:              # closes a stray menu before the re-attempt
      - keys: [esc]
        gap: 0.7
      - focus: click-center

spec.description: doomgeneric (Win32 GDI backend) + shareware WAD — adversarial-compat demo

olewinetest.yaml:
# Wine's own ole32/oleaut32 conformance suites, run by the apitest sweep runner.
#
# Why this exists: ole32 and oleaut32 are Rust ports of the PRE-wine-10.0 C, and
# upstream's wine-10.0 syncs (5f6b295cb90, e05d78ede06) landed on the dead C
# afterwards. Porting that delta needs a before/after oracle, and the best one
# is Wine's own tests for exactly these modules. The full rostests corpus is
# not a usable vehicle (--rostests does not build on every arch, and it stages
# 128 suites), so this payload stages just the two suites from a build dir that
# has them (any earlier `vibeos-cli build --arch X --rostests`) and reuses the
# apitest sweep runner, which already pipes each child's stdout to serial as
# [APITEST:<suite> <subtest>] lines.
#
# Wine test executables do nothing useful without a subtest name, so the list
# is one `<suite>.exe <subtest>` line per test: gen_suites.py reads each
# suite's testlist.c.
name: olewinetest
description: Wine ole32 + oleaut32 conformance suites under the apitest sweep runner

build_hint: "tools/payloads/apitest/build.sh {arch} && ./vibeos-cli build --arch {arch} --rostests --keep-going && python3 tools/payloads/olewinetest/gen_suites.py --arch {arch}"

binaries:
  - src: tools/payloads/apitest/apitest-sweep-{arch}.exe
    root: image
    dest: ProgramData/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup/apitest-sweep.exe
  - src: tools/payloads/olewinetest/winetest-suites-{arch}.txt
    dest: bin/apitest-suites.txt
  - src: tools/payloads/olewinetest/winetest-skip-{arch}.txt
    dest: bin/apitest-skip.txt
  # Children start on the writable FAT scratch disk: X: is the CDFS boot image,
  # and typelib/vartype create their test typelibs with GetTempFileName(".").
  - src: tools/payloads/olewinetest/cwd.txt
    dest: bin/apitest-cwd.txt
  - src: build-{arch}/modules/rostests/winetests/oleaut32/oleaut32_winetest.exe
    dest: bin/oleaut32_winetest.exe
  - src: build-{arch}/modules/rostests/winetests/ole32/ole32_winetest.exe
    dest: bin/ole32_winetest.exe
  # The live CD's hives are prebuilt and never run DllRegisterServer (syssetup's
  # RegisterDlls is an install step), so the classes these suites create
  # (CLSID_StdFont, StdPicture, the PS factories) are absent and the tests fail
  # on REGDB_E_CLASSNOTREG instead of on our code. The list opens by
  # registering both DLLs, as an installed system already has.
  - src: build-{arch}/base/system/regsvr32/regsvr32.exe
    dest: bin/regsvr32.exe
  # gen_suites.py --global-flag writes reg.exe steps (page heap etc. per suite).
  - src: build-{arch}/base/applications/cmdutils/reg/reg.exe
    dest: bin/reg.exe

test:
  launch_marker: "[APITEST-SWEEP] done"
  launch_drain_secs: 3600
  launch_idle_secs: 600

spec.name: olewinetest
spec.description: Wine ole32 + oleaut32 conformance suites under the apitest sweep runner

# procstorm — #39 amplifier (smp-bringup lane).
#
# The #39 wedge fires at most once per boot at the first user-mode service
# start, near a 2% rate, so soaking costs ~50 boots per sample. The evidence
# points at PROCESS CREATION as the rare event (the offending protection mask
# is 0 = MM_ZERO_ACCESS, a field nobody filled in, produced while building a
# fresh address space), so this payload builds address spaces in bulk: it
# spawns itself as a do-nothing child N times (VIBEOS_PROCSTORM_N, default
# 1000) from the All Users Startup folder.
#
# A clean storm is a real result, not a null one: it says the bug needs
# something specific to the first service start rather than process creation
# in general.
name: procstorm
description: spawn N throwaway processes to amplify the #39 address-space-setup wedge

build_hint: "tools/payloads/procstorm/build.sh {arch}"

binaries:
  - src: tools/payloads/procstorm/procstorm-{arch}.exe
    root: image
    dest: ProgramData/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup/procstorm.exe

test:
  # launch_drain_secs is WALL-CLOCK SECONDS. It used to be a read-iteration
  # count -- serial_output(timeout=1.0) returns immediately when bytes are
  # already waiting, so a chatty payload burned the budget in a fraction of the
  # stated time. This payload is the chattiest there is (every spawn makes the
  # kernel's own [PS] tracing emit a burst) and hit it first: 2400 "seconds"
  # were spent in 175s, cutting the storm off at 500/1000. The number below was
  # inflated to 60000 to compensate; test_payload.py now bounds the drain by the
  # clock, so it is back to a real duration. The marker ends the boot early.
  launch_marker: "[PROCSTORM] done"
  launch_drain_secs: 1800

regcapture.yaml:
# regcapture — what does setup's COM registration phase WRITE, per DLL?
#
# Runs syssetup.inf's registration sections ([EarlyRegisterDlls], [OleControlDlls],
# [TypeLibraries]) in-guest, each entry in a child process against an in-process registry
# sandbox (RegOverridePredefKey, as ../regdiff does), and streams what each wrote as INF AddReg
# lines. The per-entry "lines=N" is the point: it is how ole32's DllRegisterServer was found
# writing NOTHING while returning S_OK (its registry resources had been lost in an upstream
# sync; tools/test_wine_registry_resources.py now guards that).
#   tools/payloads/regcapture/build.sh <arch>
#   VIBEOS_PAYLOAD=regcapture ./vibeos-cli build --arch <arch>
#   VIBEOS_QEMU_MAX_LIFETIME=10800 ./vibeos-cli smoke --arch <arch> --payload regcapture
name: regcapture
description: run syssetup.inf's registration sections in a sandbox and stream the writes as INF

build_hint: "tools/payloads/regcapture/build.sh {arch}"

binaries:
  - src: tools/payloads/regcapture/regcapture-{arch}.exe
    root: image
    dest: ProgramData/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup/regcapture.exe
  # The capture reads the registration list from the image's own syssetup.inf, and the
  # curated arm64 ramdisk does not carry one. Same file everywhere, so staging it is harmless.
  - src: media/inf/syssetup.inf
    dest: inf/syssetup.inf

test:
  launch_marker: "[REGCAP] done"
  # ~50s per DLL under TCG (a child process each, and every line crosses the serial port),
  # so a full capture outlives the default 30-minute QEMU lifetime: run it with
  # VIBEOS_QEMU_MAX_LIFETIME=10800.
  launch_drain_secs: 10800

regdiff.yaml:
# regdiff — does a DLL's replacement register the same thing?
#
# Retiring shell32.cpp moved shell32's DllRegisterServer from ATL's static registrar
# (compiled into the C++) to atl100.dll's registrar parsing the same .rgs scripts. The media's
# hives are prebuilt, so no boot ever exercises that path; this payload measures it instead.

ucrtdiff.yaml:
# ucrtdiff — Tier 2 ucrt difftest payload.
#
# Grades our shipping ucrtbase.dll against the genuine Microsoft UCRT C, IN THE
# GUEST, where both sides are Windows and `long` is 32 bits on every arch. The
# host tier (sdk/lib/rust/ucrt-difftest) cannot reach these families at all: it
# runs on Linux, where `long` is 64 bits, which silently mis-grades ~188 public
# declarations including the whole strtol/atol family.
#
# The exe links two implementations of the same exports -- libucrt_ref.a
# (Microsoft's objects, exports renamed ref_* by tools/ucrt_tier2_refset.py)
# and the ucrtbase import lib -- so `ref_strtol` is Microsoft's body and
# `strtol` is whatever we ship. Design:
# docs/engineering/active-lanes/ucrt-tier2-difftest-design.md.
#
# GUI subsystem and a direct ucrtbase.dll import are both enforced by build.sh:
# a console exe launched from explorer's startup walk gets no CSRSS console and
# dies silently, and linking the api-ms-win-crt-* sets instead of ucrtbase.dll
# would make the bare side stop being OUR DLL -- the harness would then grade
# Microsoft's C against Microsoft's C and pass vacuously.
name: ucrtdiff
description: Tier 2 ucrt difftest — shipping ucrtbase.dll vs the genuine Microsoft C, in-guest

build_hint: "tools/payloads/ucrtdiff/build.sh {arch}"

binaries:
  - src: tools/payloads/ucrtdiff/ucrtdiff-{arch}.exe
    root: image
    dest: ProgramData/Microsoft/Windows/Start Menu/Programs/Startup/ucrtdiff.exe

test:
  # The drain is a READ-ITERATION count, not seconds (see procstorm's note), and
  # the loop returns immediately whenever bytes are already waiting -- so a CHATTY
  # payload burns iterations fast. This one emits a progress line per export plus a
  # line per failing row, and 224 exports swept over the full corpora is a lot of
  # both, so 3000 was plainly too low. NOTE it is NOT established that this is what
  # ends the run: raising it to 60000 did not move the stopping point, which is still
  # export 39. What IS established is that the harness no longer CRASHES there -- when
  # a body really dies the system keeps logging after it (17 further lines), and since
  # the thread-state fix the serial log instead ENDS at the last [UCRTDIFF] line (1),
  # which is the signature of the boot being cut off rather than the payload faulting.
  # The remaining suspect is total runtime against the VM lifetime, not this counter.
  launch_marker: "[UCRTDIFF] done"
  # WALL-CLOCK seconds since drain_for_marker was fixed (the note above predates it):
  # 60000 meant 16.7 hours, and it also sets pytest's --timeout, so the 2026-09-26
  # marker-eating hang ran each shard to the full VM lifetime. A shard's own budget is
  # UCRTDIFF_BUDGET_MS (420 s by default); this is that plus boot-to-launch slack.
  launch_drain_secs: 900

spec.name: ucrtdiff
spec.description: Tier 2 ucrt difftest — shipping ucrtbase.dll vs the genuine Microsoft C, in-guest
